sector_model: Branded small home appliances (Shark, Ninja): P/E and FCF after capex with refund and tariff effects normalized, working capital (receivables, inventory), customer concentration, leverage.
thesis: SharkNinja (NYSE: SN). Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-11-04) read in relevant sections. Q3 net sales 1,976.4M (+21.2%), 9M 5,154.7M (+19.9%); Q3 net income 338.4M vs 188.7M. Q3 gross margin 59.2% includes 243.8M of accepted IEEPA tariff refund claims booked as a reduction of cost of sales, less 45.2M payable to factory partners, plus 10.5M of related interest income; 186.1M was a receivable at 9/30 and was received in October 2026. Without the net 198.6M gross profit benefit and interest, Q3 operating income would be about 244M (442.9M less 198.6M net refund benefit, own arithmetic) versus 262.9M a year earlier, i.e. down about 7% despite sales +21%. 9M OCF only 107.4M against 589.6M net income because receivables (-460.8M), inventories (-436.2M) and prepaids (-282.7M) rose, partly offset by payables and accruals (+431M). Cash 487.8M vs term loan 708.75M; 169.7M of buybacks in 9M. Close 212.64 x 140.91M shares = 29.96B: about 35.5x TTM reported NI 844.9M, about 44x excluding an estimated 161M after-tax refund benefit (own approximation, 23% tax rate), FCF yield about 1.6%, 9.5x book.
counterthesis: The reported profit surge is mostly a one-time refund; underlying Q3 operating income appears lower year on year while selling, marketing and G&A grew faster than sales. Cash conversion is weak (9M OCF 18% of NI) and the customer concentration is high (Customer A 23.4% of Q3 sales and 28.8% of receivables). SBC jumped to 119.6M from 31.6M in 9M. The valuation (about 44x normalized earnings, 1.6% FCF yield) already prices continued 20% growth and margin recovery.
invalidation: Invalidated as a value idea if normalized earnings do not grow into the multiple; supported only if working capital reverses into strong Q4 cash flow and growth stays near 20% without refund help. Thesis breakers: sales growth under 10%, further tariff shocks, loss of the major retail customer, receivable build continuing.
